reduction.quote: making all pieces equal to 1/(2n+1). Then Liu Bang gets n+1 pieces out of 2n+1, totaling (n+1)/(2n+1).
reduction.witness: Missing statement: a proof that in the claiming phase both players optimally take the currently largest remaining piece, so that the outcome equals the alternating sum of the piece lengths sorted in decreasing order (Liu getting ranks 1,3,5,...). The quoted passage only counts pieces in one specific all-equal configuration and never analyses the greedy/alternating-sum structure of the claiming game in general.
reduction.load_bearing: Every bound on the value of the game requires knowing what the claiming phase yields for an arbitrary multiset of pieces; the text only tallies pieces in a single symmetric example.

lower_bound.quote: Attempted to compute X's optimal response to L's marks via discretized search; results suggest L can guarantee at least (n+1)/(2n+1) by placing marks at 1/(2n+1), 2/(2n+1), ..., n/(2n+1).
lower_bound.witness: Missing statement: an explicit Liu division together with a proof, valid for every n and every one of Xiang Yu's at most n replies (arbitrary interleaving of new cuts), that Liu's alternating-sum total is at least c. The quoted passage reports only discretized numerical search on a guessed division and proves nothing; moreover the proposed target (n+1)/(2n+1) exceeds the true value 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) for n>=3, so no such proof exists for it.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The claimed guarantee for Liu rests entirely on this unproved numerical observation; no strategy argument covering arbitrary Xiang replies appears anywhere in the text.
